stage_2_story.text_en:
The night before the Maccabiah regional championship, Lior sat next to his grandfather Moshe at the kitchen table. Lior was sixteen and had been training five mornings a week for two years. Moshe wanted to understand.

'Explain to me,' Moshe said, placing his tea down. 'What exactly happens tomorrow?'

Lior opened his notebook. 'I swim the two-hundred individual medley, Saba. That means all four strokes — butterfly first, then backstroke, breaststroke, and freestyle at the end. One hundred and fifty metres of suffering,' he smiled.

'What has the coach told you to do differently this week?' Moshe asked. 'We are in taper,' Lior said. 'We trained much less — shorter sessions, easy distances. The body rests and feels strong again. It sounds like doing nothing, but it is very scientific.'

'And in the race itself?' Lior pulled out a printed sheet with numbers on it. 'This is my split time plan. I need to finish the butterfly fifty metres in thirty-two seconds. If I check the pace clock at the turn and I am too slow, I know I need to push harder.'

Moshe pointed to a drawing of a swimmer at the wall. 'What is this?' 'That is the tumble turn, Saba. At every wall, instead of stopping, you flip, plant your feet, and push off underwater. A bad tumble turn can cost you half a second — a good one gives you speed for free.'

'And how do you go faster?' Moshe asked. Lior thought for a moment. 'Three things. A high stroke rate so I do not slow down in the middle. A strong pull under the water — that is where the real power comes from. And good kick to keep my legs up so there is less drag. If I do all three, I have a chance.'

Moshe nodded slowly. 'You sound like an engineer.' Lior laughed. 'Swimming is engineering, Saba. Come tomorrow and you will see.'
